senses.gloss: , נִימּוֹס, נִימַּס to melt, be liquefied; to fall away; to faint; to despair.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 25">Ex. R. s. 25</cite> <he>נִימּוֹסִּין</he> (Var. <he>נִימַּסִּין</he>) they faint.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 251:14">Yalk. ib. 251</cite> <he>התחילו נְמַסִּין</he> they began to lose heart; Mekh. B’shall., Shir., s. 9 <he>לֵהָמֵס</he>.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 1">Deut. R. s. 1</cite>, end <he>תִּימַּס עינו וכ׳</he> may this man’s (thy) eye run out.

Maasr. I, 2 הרמונים משיִמַּסּוּ pomegranates are subject to tithes when their core becomes pulpy; expl. Y. ib. 48ᵈ bot. משיתמעך אוכל וכ׳ (cmp. מִסְמֵס II) when the eatable portion (core) can be mashed under one’s fingers; [anoth. definition taking our w. in the sense of falling away, diminution; משיכניסו מחצה when the ripening core is reduced to half the capacity of the cavity,—upon which the remark is made, דילמא … הֵמַסּוּ … פלגון לבבנו perhaps he learned it from the homiletical teachers who interpret hemassu &c. (Deut. I, 28), they divided our hearts (an allusion to Num. R. s. 17)].

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite>, beg. (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 39:12">Ps. XXXIX, 12</cite>) <he>כל חמדה … הֵמַסְתָּ אותה וכ׳</he> (not <he>אותו</he>) all the delight which Moses longed for, to enter the land,—thou hast caused it to decay as a moth enters garments and makes them decay. V. <cite ref="M01852"><he>מָסָה</he></cite>.
